program: Prospective safer-corridor design and timing within the whole cycling portfolio

nutshell.headline: A real forward-looking design opportunity, but no verified marginal safety yield
nutshell.body: The research list uses the central scenario: $239,958,108 per 10 Bay QALYs. Signed prior-weighted estimate: $38,112,941 per10 Bay QALYs; 0.0002623780702421395 QALYs per illustrative$1,000. Central world: $239,958,108. This is prospective infrastructure-safety health at full organization cost, not all SVBC benefits or a measured giving return.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Technical input and community knowledge can improve which crossings are built, their protection, and timing. Safety changes can benefit many users and draw on public implementation resources.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The favorable5% world generates 97.2% of signed expected health; without it the estimate is $1,300,569,697. Even that favorable world costs $1,960,219 per10. Site-specific crash exposure, changed implementation and donor contribution are priors.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD giving recommendation. Need the particular unresolved design/timing decision, its injury baseline, SVBC contribution and dated additional work an unrestricted gift would purchase.

programSection.body: SVBC is EIN77-0338658, serving Santa Clara/San Mateo with regional Bay cycling programs. Education, events, organizing and public-agency engagement share the ordinary budget. Model concentrates on prospective design or acceleration, not electoral persuasion, past lane wins or event attendance.

steps.title: Support the whole organization
steps.detail: One annual whole-budget-equivalent supports a hypothetical portfolio of future infrastructure changes. No repeat credit for the same project every funding year.

steps.title: Change implementation beyond the baseline
steps.detail: Organization contribution is separate from donor cash response. Public planners, funding, engineers, other advocates and eventual construction remain causal partners and alternatives.

steps.title: Count finite safety effects
steps.detail: Reduce fatal and disjoint serious nonfatal incident rates during a bounded advantage window, discount implementation lag, and assign finite post-event health. An adverse-design world permits net harm.

programSection.boundary: Whole donor-accounting cost, partial health. Public construction/maintenance, funded planning and volunteer inputs are not free societal resources; incremental costs unknown. Bay shares.9–.98 are judgments about affected users, not headquarters attribution. Education, sustained physical activity, transport access and other benefits remain unquantified; not a complete-return claim or guaranteed lower bound.

model.headline: $38,112,941 per10 Bay QALYs
model.body: Weights locked before first execution: funding-null25%, implementation-null20%, adverse-design10%, cautious20%, central20%, favorable5%. Expected signed QALYs calculated before inversion; no coefficients changed after the unfavorable first result. These weights are not calibrated probabilities.

equation.label: Finite prospective safety portfolio
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × organization contribution × donor response × Bay share × net safety reduction × discounted advantage-years × [annual fatal events × finite survival QALYs + annual serious nonfatal events × finite injury QALYs]

inputs.label: Whole operating boundary
inputs.basis: Original PartsVIII/IX addbacks retained. Unrestricted netassets$671,427 and about$1.021M cash/savings do not prove current spendable capacity.

inputs.label: Annual incidents in actually changed sites
inputs.basis: Explicit prospective portfolio priors, NOT observed corridor counts or county totals. Event types are disjoint; no multiply by miles or class participants.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Net incident reduction
inputs.basis: Judgmental transport of heterogeneous route-safety evidence, accounting jointly for induced exposure/diversion. Not Teschke odds ratio applied as exact ARR; no duplicate crash penalty.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Advantage window / implementation lag
inputs.basis: Window ends when alternative implementation catches up; not full asset life. Lag is discounted. No permanent benefit from plan adoption.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: SVBC causal share
inputs.basis: Joint expected contribution of this annual-budget work cohort: includes the probability the changed design is actually built and its share beyond agencies, other advocates, and SVBC's own past/future funded work. Future SVBC effort is not free. This coefficient is not total multiyear SVBC credit; realization is embedded here rather than multiplied again. Unverified judgment.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Additional response to ordinary gift
inputs.basis: Budget-level substitution/capacity and portfolio-allocation judgment, separate from organization contribution.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Finite remaining life10years, utility.8, hazard.03
inputs.basis: Analyst health-state/remaining-life priors; no age-specific local crash-survivor estimate. Integrate utility×exp(−(hazard+ln1.03)t).
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Nonfatal injury loss avoided
inputs.basis: Serious injuries only, disjoint from deaths; injury-level severity/duration unobserved locally. Discount integral, not hospital bills as health.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

inputs.label: Bay resident-health fraction
inputs.basis: Local project geography does not prove every affected user is a Bay resident.
inputs.confidence: Very low, analyst prior rather than observed local effect

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Exposure integral runs from implementation lag through lag+advantage years; per-event health is additionally finite, up to15years after avoided fatality and2years after injury in default worlds. Fatal and nonfatal outcomes do not overlap. No causal local before/after outcome or incremental retained-cyclist count identified. Values are research priors, not actuarial precision. Attribution includes implementation realization and dilution by SVBC's own separately funded past/future work. One annual budget does not purchase all multiyear advocacy or guarantee construction.
model.fundingBoundary: VTA ABC public plan already has$880,000 funding ($695,200 Caltrans plus$184,800 local match), with concepts/cost estimates scheduledSeptember2026 and final planSpring2027. SVBC August2026 restructuring offers local-team support and microgrant review fromOctober; it does not establish an unfunded construction tranche. Existing annual return includes large regional event activity; all of it stays costed. Ask (1) which still-open design/timing decision extra staff work changes; (2) site-specific baseline risk, alternative design/date and partner commitments; (3) additional work purchasable with$1,000 beyond current resources and what happens if no gift. No verified giving checkout reviewed; donationUrl omitted.

evidence.design: Case-crossover study of route injury risk
evidence.result: Cycle tracks adjustedOR.11,95%CI.02–.54 versus major streets with parked cars/no cycling infrastructure.
evidence.transfer: Within-trip comparison controls personal/trip factors but not randomized local construction; no precise fatality reduction or SVBC contribution inferred.

evidence.design: Primary US three-city case-crossover study, publisher abstract
evidence.result: Heavy separationOR.10(.01–.95); lighter one-way separationOR1.19(.46–3.10); two-wayOR11.38(1.40–92.57), largely one lane.
evidence.transfer: Design heterogeneity and possible harm prevent universal protected-lane effect. Full text not retrieved in this phase; use as disconfirmation, not direct numerical calibration.

evidence.design: Public grant proposal and annual filing outputs
evidence.result: FY2026 grant metrics are proposed targets, not observed additional sustained activity. Class counts and challenge miles establish delivery only.
evidence.transfer: No exercise mortality benefit assigned without retained incremental activity, displacement and health-risk mapping.
